motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Declare April 25 as Arbor Day
motions.summary: The council proclaimed April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: Symbolic only — nothing changes for residents.

motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April as Financial Literacy Month
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April as Financial Literacy Month. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Declare April Financial Literacy Month
motions.summary: The council proclaimed April as Financial Literacy Month in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: This is a symbolic declaration with no rules or spending attached — nothing changes for residents.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Marian Burningham for a three year term, through December 31, 2027,…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the appointment of Marian Burningham for a three year term, through December 31, 2027, to the Cemetery Advisory Board. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Appoint Marian Burningham to cemetery board
motions.summary: The council appointed Marian Burningham to a three-year term on the Cemetery Advisory Board, running through December 31, 2027.
motions.impact: A routine volunteer appointment — nothing changes for residents day to day.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing item 14.A. to be addressed in the scheduled items. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion. Councilmember Gray requested that the correction to the minutes be included in the motion. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing 14.A. to be addressed in the scheduled items and including the adjustments to the March 18, 2025 minutes as noted from Councilmember Gray in the Work Session. Councilmember Wood seconded the amended motion.
motions.headline: Approve the routine consent agenda
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, pulling one item out for separate discussion and folding in corrections to the March 18 minutes.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents.

motions.item_title: Approve the UTA Park and ride Site Plan as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the UTA Park and ride Site Plan as presented. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve a park-and-ride lot for transit riders
motions.summary: The council approved the site plan for a Utah Transit Authority park-and-ride lot in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: If you commute by bus, the city will eventually have a place to park and catch transit. The motion does not say where it goes or when it opens.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Releasing a Permanent Sanitary Sewer Easement and Retaining a Temporary Sanitary Sewer Easement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Releasing a Permanent Sanitary Sewer Easement and Retaining a Temporary Sanitary Sewer Easement. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Give up a permanent sewer easement
motions.summary: The city released a permanent sewer easement while keeping a temporary one in place.
motions.impact: Routine property paperwork touching a single parcel — nothing changes for residents.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Update the long-range map for Big Eagle 7
motions.summary: The council changed the city's long-range future land use map for the Big Eagle 7 area.
motions.impact: This is the follow-up paperwork that keeps the city's long-range plan consistent with the rezoning of the same land — no separate change for residents.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial base zoning and apply the RTI overlay zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial base zoning and apply the RTI overlay zone. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rezone Big Eagle 7 land for industry
motions.summary: The city rezoned the land known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial zoning and applied an additional overlay zone on top of it.
motions.impact: Industrial development is now allowed on this land. If you live near Big Eagle 7, expect industrial buildings rather than homes as the area builds out.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Zoning as presented in the updated packet
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Zoning as presented in the updated packet. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Update the city's zoning rules
motions.summary: The council approved changes to the city's zoning code, Title 17, as laid out in the updated meeting packet.
motions.impact: The motion itself does not spell out what changed, so the effect depends on the packet details. Zoning rules govern what can be built and where in the city.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: failed for lack of majority vote; 2:3.
motions.headline: Inland port project area rejected
motions.summary: The council declined to support creating a state Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: No inland port district moves forward in the city for now, and nothing changes on the ground. The state authority would need the city's backing to proceed here.

motions.item_title: Adopt implementation of the MBR technology solution and the use of CM/CG construction methodolo…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt implementation of the MBR technology solution and the use of CM/CG construction methodology for the proposed sewer treatment facility. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Pick the technology for the new sewer plant
motions.summary: The city chose membrane filtration treatment technology and a construction-manager delivery method for its proposed sewer plant.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now. This is a technical choice about how the future sewer plant will treat waste and how it will be built, made before design begins.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved authorize staff to begin analysis and preparation for a potential future action to place a Recreation, Arts, and Parks (RAP) Sales Tax question on the 2025 Municipal Election ballot. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Study a sales tax for parks and arts
motions.summary: The council directed staff to study whether to put a Recreation, Arts, and Parks sales tax question on the 2025 city election ballot.
motions.impact: No new tax yet — this is only groundwork. If the council goes ahead, you would be the one voting on it in the 2025 city election.

motions.item_title: The Completed Section of the Legislative Priority List and also add Design of City Hall and oth…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved that the City Hall Land Acquisition and Mortgage Assistance Program items be moved to the Completed Section of the Legislative Priority List and also add Design of City Hall and other uses within Phase 1 of the Downtown Plan as a High Priority to the list. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Make City Hall design a top priority
motions.summary: The council marked the City Hall land purchase and a mortgage help program as finished, and made designing City Hall a high priority for the year ahead.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you today — this is the city's internal to-do list. It signals City Hall and the first phase of the downtown plan are next in line for work.
